note: Operator angle. Several elegance HOLDs are still in the near-term snippets Foreman would implement; those contradictions are treated as the spec, not as already-fixed.

findings.criterion: A finished run registers itself — the row carries the roadmap step it belongs to (the active step at the time); Both places, one source — the outline lists the step's register rows
findings.message: The surface John locked is: open the roadmap step, click the report. Criterion 1 requires the step on the row; criterion 3 keys the outline on that column; P2.4 exists only to fill it. The implementation-facing snippets for the two examples he named — Gandalf (Hook A) and classic lane jobs (Hook B) — call `register(...)` with what/where/date and never pass `step`. `register()` is specified as appending the facts it is given; it does not say it will call `active_step` when step is omitted. Hook C is the only hook that even mentions a step hint. A builder copying those snippets ships rows the tile can show and the outline cannot match. That is today's bug, half-fixed: the report still does not appear under the step he opens.

findings.criterion: A finished run registers itself — when a run finishes, one row is appended; the deliverable section is where the human-facing report is clicked
findings.message: Criterion 1 is one row when a run finishes — the report, the plan, the execution log. Hook C's near-term text registers "for each doc the session persisted (`efforts_for_session_id` + `session_doc_roles`)." That dumps agent, provenance, and raw session files into the same list John uses to click the report. The parenthetical HOLD ("human-facing report/plan/execlog only") is not the snippet. Operator result: the deliverable section and the step expansion fill with computer-facing paths; the thing he asked for is one line among junk. The `finish_run` hook is required. The per-doc blast makes the register unusable as a click target.

findings.section: Phase 2 — Hook B / Hook C′ / Deferred
findings.criterion: A finished run registers itself — when a Foreman wave GOes, one row is appended; the statement names a Foreman execution log as a clickable link
findings.message: The locked criterion names three finish events: Gandalf finalizes, a researchPrime/lane job finishes, **or a Foreman wave GOes**. The statement names the execution log as a link. The plan then (a) filters Hook B to `lane in ('research','plan')` so a classic build/lane job writes nothing, (b) defers uncommissioned terminal Foreman so close/kill writes nothing, and (c) parks Hook C′ — the only wave-GO writer — behind a question. What remains is steward-commissioned Foreman, one execlog row at `finish_run`. If John ran the build from the project window — the path the risk table itself keeps in scope — the outline and the tile never get the log. That is not a follow-on and not a question. It is the named Foreman artifact missing on a launch path he actually uses. Commit a Foreman writer on the paths criterion 1 named, or the third finish event is fiction.

findings.criterion: A runnable deliverable has a Run link — the control opens a cockpit terminal with the command staged
findings.message: Criterion 4 is a Run link that opens a terminal. Phase 1's near-term still adds `Run ▶` wired to a no-op that `textContent`s the command. A control labeled Run that does not run is a false affordance: he clicks it, sees the command as text, and concludes it is broken — or that it already ran. The HOLD ("wire Run ▶ in the same change as P3.4") is correct and has not deleted the no-op from the spec. Do not put a Run control on the page until the POST exists. The Open link can ship in Phase 1; Run cannot.

findings.criterion: Both places, one source — a report registered with a step shows in the plan outline; the deliverables tile always shows it
findings.message: The risk table sends classic window jobs to the project root. Hook B does the same (`rec.get('effort_dir') or project root`). The plan outline reads the **effort's** `DELIVERABLES.md`. A project that has an effort — the case John works in — then has the report in the project-root file / project-wide list, not under the effort step he opens. Criterion 3 is both places, not "the tile if the row landed in the file that list happens to read." The mitigation ("project root is the effort of record") solves where to write and abandons "open the step and click." Steward-commissioned runs are fine (campaign dir). The classic path the risk table keeps in scope still leaves the outline empty.

findings.topic: Run cwd is effort dir not project tree
findings.criterion: A runnable deliverable has a Run link — a cockpit terminal in the project's tree with the command staged, Enter to run
findings.message: The locked Run behavior is a terminal **in the project's tree**. The decision text already hedges "project tree or the row's effort dir"; the endpoint then sets cwd to "that row's effort dir when the row is effort-level." A `run: python tools/foo.py` written against the project root fails on Enter when cwd is `planning/…/effort`. He pressed Enter; it did not run. That is the operator failure criterion 4 exists to prevent. The allowlist should stage the command; cwd must be the project folder the North Star named, unless the row itself declares otherwise.

findings.topic: shell pending-paste flushes on first bytes
findings.criterion: A runnable deliverable has a Run link — the command staged as a pending paste, Enter runs it; Nothing regresses, and it is seen — Playwright shows the command sitting unsent on the prompt
findings.message: Criterion 4/5 require the command sitting unsent on the prompt so Enter runs it. For `backend=='shell'` the flush condition is "first prompt bytes (any output)." A Windows PowerShell/`COMSPEC` banner is output that is not a prompt. Flushing raw command bytes into the banner means he does not see a clean staged line — and may not have a runnable command on the prompt at all. The existing greet-gated flush exists because "any output" is the wrong gate. Phase 4's screenshot ("command sitting unsent on the prompt") will either fail honestly or pass against a stub with no banner. Name a real idle-prompt detector before claiming Enter-to-run.

findings.criterion: A runnable deliverable has a Run link — an Anchor window, token-gated
findings.message: Every GET terminal transport here is token-gated (`?token=`). Phase 1's Open link specifies appending the token the way the file link already does. The Run path opens `/terminal?session=<sid>` and does not mention the token. 401-before-substance is already the law: he clicks Run ▶, a window opens, and it is blank. Criterion 4's Anchor window never appears. Carry the token the same way the Open link does, or the first time anyone notices is the Phase 4 screenshot of an empty page.

findings.topic: registrar miss is silent on the page
findings.criterion: A finished run registers itself; Nothing regresses, and it is seen
findings.message: Criterion 1 is a row appearing; criterion 5 is that it is seen. `register()` "Never raises (best-effort, returns the reason)." The only observer of a miss is a journal payload `{register: written|dup|reason}` he does not read. A finish that returns `written:false` leaves the outline and the tile exactly as they are today — no link — with no cockpit signal. Best-effort is right (a registrar exception must not fail the job). Operator-visible success cannot be only a journal field. Surface the miss on the effort, or fail the Phase 4 dogfood when the row is absent; otherwise "it is seen" is unenforceable the first time a hook no-ops in production.

findings.criterion: Both places, one source — the pane and the plan outline render the same register rows as links
findings.message: The register is one source; the paint is two (shared.js `delivRow` for tile+outline, cockpit.html `loadDeliv` for the project-wide list), each getting its own route branch. The plan already admits that leaving `loadDeliv` unpatched makes the same row a link in the tile and dead text in the other list. That failure returns the day the two copies diverge. Make `loadDeliv` call `delivRow` (or one helper). Two hand-kept route branches are how one of the two places goes dark.

findings.criterion: A runnable deliverable has a Run link — a Where/How cell declares run: <command>; non-goal: no schema change to DELIVERABLES.md beyond an optional cell
findings.message: Parsing `run:` from the existing Where cell is required. Scanning "an optional 5th 'How' column if present" is the schema change the North Star parked. He does not need a fifth column to click Run. Keep `run:` in Where; drop the extra-column scan.
